ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, from left to right there are four different figures. The 1st is a circle crossed by a horizontal line, and the horizontal line extends out on both the left and right sides of the circle. The 2nd is a circle, with a short horizontal segment attached to each of the left and right sides, but there is no horizontal line segment inside the circle. The 3rd is two concentric circles, crossed by a horizontal line and extending out on both sides of the outer circle. The 4th is three concentric circles, also crossed by a horizontal line and extending out on both sides of the outer circle. Reasoning: Regard each figure as a graph in graph theory, with all intersections, contact points, and segment endpoints as vertices, and arc segments and straight-line segments as edges. A connected graph can be drawn in one stroke without repeating edges if and only if the number of odd-degree vertices is 0 or 2. In the 1st figure, the degrees of the intersections of the circle and the horizontal line are even, and only the two free endpoints of the horizontal line are odd-degree vertices, so it can be drawn in one stroke. In the 2nd figure, the free endpoints of the two short lines on the left and right are odd-degree vertices, and at the contact points of the two short lines with the circle, two circular arcs and one short line meet, so the degree is 3, also odd-degree vertices; there are 4 odd-degree vertices in total, so it cannot be drawn in one stroke. In the 3rd figure, the degrees of the intersections of each circle and the horizontal line are all even, and only the two ends of the horizontal line are odd-degree vertices, so it can be drawn in one stroke. The 4th figure is the same; all circle-line intersections are even-degree, and only the two ends of the horizontal line are odd-degree vertices, so it can be drawn in one stroke. Therefore, there are 3 figures that can be drawn in one stroke.

raw_record.question_text: How many of the figures shown can be drawn with one continuous line without drawing a segment twice?

method.method_draft: Model each shown figure as a graph and apply the Euler-trail criterion. From the image, identify four figures: (1) one circle cut by a horizontal line extending past both sides, (2) one circle with only two short horizontal stubs attached at left and right, (3) two concentric circles cut by a horizontal line, and (4) three concentric circles cut by a horizontal line. Treat every intersection, contact point, and free line endpoint as a graph vertex; arcs and straight pieces between vertices are graph edges. From the text, the task is to count figures drawable in one continuous stroke without repeating an edge. Use the rule: a connected graph has such a drawing iff it has exactly 0 or 2 vertices of odd degree. Figure 1 has only the two free horizontal endpoints odd, so it works. Figure 2 has four odd vertices: the two stub endpoints plus the two circle-contact points of degree 3, so it does not work. Figures 3 and 4 again have only the two free horizontal endpoints odd; all circle-line crossings have even degree, so both work. Therefore 3 figures can be drawn.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：附图中从左到右有四个不同图形。第1个是一个圆被一条水平线穿过，水平线在圆的左右两侧都伸出。第2个是一个圆，左右两侧各接一小段水平短线，但圆内部没有水平线段。第3个是两个同心圆，被一条水平线穿过并伸出外圆两侧。第4个是三个同心圆，也被一条水平线穿过并伸出外圆两侧。

推理：把每个图形看成图论中的图，所有交点、接触点和线段端点作为顶点，弧段和直线段作为边。一个连通图能一笔画且不重复边，当且仅当奇度顶点数为0个或2个。第1个图形中，圆与水平线的交点度数为偶数，只有水平线的两个自由端点是奇度顶点，所以可以一笔画。第2个图形中，左右两个短线的自由端点是奇度顶点，两个短线与圆接触点各有两段圆弧和一段短线相接，度数为3，也是奇度顶点，共4个奇度顶点，所以不可以一笔画。第3个图形中，各圆与水平线的交点度数都是偶数，只有水平线两端是奇度顶点，所以可以一笔画。第4个图形同理，所有圆线交点为偶度，只有水平线两端为奇度顶点，所以可以一笔画。因此可以一笔画的图形共有3个。
